protections: P1: the ASCII-escaping encoder must reject malformed / truncated / out-of-range UTF-8 in string values AND dict keys instead of folding arbitrary bytes into \uXXXX: Buffer_EscapeStringValidated, reached for values at src/ujson/lib/ultrajsonenc.c:906-914 and for keys at src/ujson/lib/ultrajsonenc.c:690-703.
P2: the JSON string decoder must reject malformed UTF-8 in ujson.loads input instead of mapping invalid byte sequences onto arbitrary codepoints: decode_string, src/ujson/lib/ultrajsondec.c:416-587.

P3: for the ensure_ascii=False path, the only guard is the Python-boundary backstop PyUnicode_DecodeUTF8(ret, retLen, "surrogatepass") at src/ujson/python/objToJSON.c:867, applied to the whole encoder output buffer.
P4: reject_bytes=True must raise TypeError for bytes anywhere in the dumped object graph (src/ujson/python/objToJSON.c:426-438 for values; help text at src/ujson/python/ujson.c:61).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The report's example is a bad continuation byte in a 2-byte sequence; the `if (ucs < 0x10000)` test at :434 reads like the range check, so a well-formed 4-byte lead (0xf4 0x90.. and 0xf5-0xf7, all mapped to utflen 4 at :104) is assumed already valid.
Each arm already has a truncation guard (`if (end - io < 1/2/3)`), so the arm looks handled; only the boundary value is wrong, and the extra byte read lands on the NUL that PyBytes always appends.

The advisory names ujson.dumps() only; loads() is the opposite direction, and the published fix's only decoder footprint is error wording, so the decoder's own validator can be called a separate feature the advisory never covered.
A lone 0x9b in a string body reads as permissive bytes decoding rather than a UTF-8 sequence bug, and the report is about dumping bytes, not about which byte classes may start a character.
The report points at the encoder's 4-byte arm; the decoder's own codepoint range was never in the advisory and the published fix left the decoder's logic untouched.

The __json__ producer hands raw bytes straight to Buffer_memcpy with no escaping at all, but the PyUnicode_DecodeUTF8 backstop at objToJSON.c:867 already rejects malformed ones, so nothing is silently rewritten end to end.

forceASCII=0 is documented as a raw passthrough ("UTF-8 or what ever charset strings are brought as", ultrajson.h:244); in Python it is chosen by ensure_ascii=False and its output is still decoded strictly at objToJSON.c:867, while the embeddable libujson.a entry via JSON_EncodeObject cannot be reached from pytest.
reject_bytes is a bytes-policy switch, not the UTF-8 property in the advisory; bytes keys have always been coerced verbatim by Dict_convertKey and the report says nothing about them.
A strict RFC-3629 validator calls ED A0 80 malformed, so a solver can read the surrogate expectations as legacy quirks to update rather than as a value the new guard must keep accepting.

The reported repro is a top-level bytes value, so a guard added where the report lands (objToJSON.c:426-438) is assumed to cover keys too; bytes keys take the Dict_convertKey route and are exempt from reject_bytes anyway.

masking: T2 is masked by T1: once continuation bytes are validated, a broad 'malformed UTF-8 raises' test passes, and only a well-formed but >U+10FFFF 4-byte sequence (0xf4 0x90 0x80 0x80, or a 0xf5-0xf7 lead) still shows the missing range check.

T3 is masked by T1: with a continuation test added, a sequence truncated at end-of-buffer reads the trailing NUL, fails the continuation test and raises, so the one-byte-short bounds never show in a behavioural test.
T5 and T6 are masked by T4: after the continuation mask is fixed, most malformed decoder input raises, and only a lone 0x80-0xbf lead byte or a well-formed >U+10FFFF sequence still decodes.
T11 is exposed by where T1 is fixed: a guard placed only in the bytes-value branch at objToJSON.c:426-438 makes the reported value repro pass while bytes dict keys stay unvalidated.

conflicts.what: The natural strict-UTF-8 continuation/range fix also rejects D800-DFFF; that breaks tests/test_ujson.py:643-650, which require dumps(b'\xed\xa0\x80', reject_bytes=False) to yield "\ud800" (and the same bytes as a dict key). The guard must accept ED A0 80-ED BF BF.
A strict decoder that rejects surrogate codepoints breaks tests/test_ujson.py:684-686, which require loads(b'"\xed\xa0\x80"') to return a lone surrogate.
Same as T4 on the lead-byte side: a table that rejects 0xed, or any rule that rejects surrogate codepoints, breaks the decoder surrogate round-trip at tests/test_ujson.py:686.

Mirroring the validated checks into Buffer_EscapeStringUnvalidated (or decoding ensure_ascii=False output with a strict codec instead of surrogatepass) breaks tests/test_ujson.py:652-654, which require ensure_ascii=False to emit raw lone-surrogate bytes.
A key-side strict-UTF-8 check in Dict_convertKey (a natural place to add validation, objToJSON.c:214-242) rejects the UTF-8-encoded surrogate keys used at tests/test_ujson.py:648-650.

fairness_risks: Must-keep value: UTF-8-encoded lone surrogates (ED A0 80 / ED BF BF) must stay accepted and be escaped to \ud800 / \udfff - tests/test_ujson.py:643-650 (encoder, bytes keys and values) and tests/test_ujson.py:684-686 (decoder, bytes input). Strict RFC-3629 rejects the surrogate range, so 'the security rule' and the pinned test suite contradict each other unless the rule is explicitly surrogate-permitting.

Must-keep value: ensure_ascii=False must keep writing raw surrogate bytes for str input (tests/test_ujson.py:652-654); any validation added to the ensure_ascii=False branch that is stricter than PyUnicode_DecodeUTF8(..., "surrogatepass") breaks it.

Error type is load-bearing: every encoder-side SetError becomes PyExc_OverflowError (src/ujson/python/objToJSON.c:849-855; pinned test tests/test_ujson.py:374-377). A solver who raises UnicodeDecodeError or ValueError from objToJSON is defensible but would fail any test that matches the existing exception type or message.
Legitimate input shape: all valid non-ASCII UTF-8 must keep round-tripping (tests/test_ujson.py:1140-1155, 510-514); a rule that rejects bytes >= 0x80 or any multi-byte sequence is over-broad.

Legitimate input shape: ujson.loads accepts any C-contiguous buffer, including array.array and memoryview (src/ujson/python/JSONtoObj.c:204-217; tests/test_ujson.py:1468-1481 and 1504-1513). A decoder fix that requires NUL termination, or that pre-decodes the whole buffer with a Python codec, must not drop those input types.

Legitimate input shape: bytes dict keys with reject_bytes=False must keep working (tests/test_ujson.py:648-650 passes a bytes key), so a key-side guard must be UTF-8 validation rather than a bytes ban.

design.why: Five independent judgements across two implementations, each with a different dismissal. G1{T1,T3,T11} is the advisory surface, but it still holds three shapes: 2/3/4-byte continuation bytes, an end-of-buffer truncation whose guard is already there but one byte short, and the bytes-dict-key entry that bypasses the bytes-value branch where the report lands. G2{T2} needs a second rule (codepoint range) in an arm that already looks guarded by the overlong test. G3{T4} is the same class in the separate decoder implementation, where a guard exists but tests the wrong bit mask ((oct & 0x80) != 0x80) and whose only published-fix footprint is error wording - the strongest dismissable reason. G4{T5} needs the lead-byte table changed, which the mask fix does not touch. G9{T10} is the M11 keep-working value that punishes the over-strict RFC-3629 fix MiMo tends to write. The four dismissal arguments are distinct: 'it is the reported repro', 'the range guard is already there', 'loads() is the other direction and the fix only relabelled messages', and 'surrogates must survive'. T6, T7, T8 and T9 are deliberately left out: T6's end-to-end behaviour depends on unverified PyUnicode_FromKindAndData handling of >U+10FFFF; T7 and T8 are already closed end to end by the PyUnicode_DecodeUTF8 backstop, so grading a change there would reward a false positive (and T8's libujson.a leg is not reachable from pytest); T9 is a reject_bytes policy gap, not the advisory's UTF-8 property.

unverified: The full advisory text was not available; whether GHSA-3J69-69WJ-XQX2 / CVE-2026-54911 is meant to cover ujson.loads as well as ujson.dumps is judged from the screener summary, the landing point and the code, not from the report.

fix.diff was not available in the pinned worktree, so whether the published fix actually adds the encoder >U+10FFFF check (T2) and the corrected end-of-buffer bounds (T3) is inferred from the screener's fix_sites and O6 input-shape list, not read.

Whether CPython's PyUnicode_FromKindAndData (src/ujson/python/JSONtoObj.c:84) rejects or silently stores a >U+10FFFF codepoint was not verified (no build/run), so T6's end-to-end observable behaviour (raise vs a broken str) is unknown.

Whether the hidden tests assert exact hyphenated validator message text (e.g. the new continuation messages, or the decoder's 'Overlong 3 byte ... when encoding string' wording at src/ujson/lib/ultrajsondec.c:557 that the published fix is said to have relabelled) is unknown; a message-only hunk is not a trap under the mechanism rules but would be graded if asserted.

No git history access in this session: whether the existing overlong checks (ultrajsonenc.c:371-376, 407-412, 434-439) and 'Unterminated UTF-8 sequence' bounds came from an earlier fix commit - which would make this an H3b incomplete-fix shape rather than a pure H4 - could not be confirmed.

The extension was not compiled and no tests were run; all behaviour is read off the C sources. That a new encoder SetError surfaces as PyExc_OverflowError follows from src/ujson/python/objToJSON.c:849-855 and matches the pinned expectation at tests/test_ujson.py:374-377, but was not executed.

The decoder's reliance on a trailing NUL (it reads *ds->start / *inputOffset without an end check at ultrajsondec.c:418, 521, 547, 570) is only safe for NUL-terminated inputs; whether array.array/memoryview inputs (accepted at JSONtoObj.c:204-217, exercised at tests/test_ujson.py:1478-1481) read out of bounds was not measured, and it is a separate bounds family rather than the UTF-8 property.

Whether the encoder's one-byte-over reads at ultrajsonenc.c:362/395/428 stay inside the allocation depends on the NUL that PyBytes and PyUnicode_AsEncodedString append; this holds for the Python bindings but not for an arbitrary caller of the C API, and was not checked under ASAN.
